question: does the partial projection exclude only the root-of-unity sublocus, or the whole fibre locus?
answer: the whole fibre locus. Reality is a condition at every point of |q| = 1 and has exactly four solutions {0, pi/3, pi, 5pi/3}, all degenerate. With the full projection imposing nothing, route 5's N-selection mechanism predicts nothing under either reading.
scope: (a), conditional on the reality assumption route 5's N-selection already rests on (that Q_beta must be real AT the fibre evaluation point, not merely after the archimedean functor). Not a refutation of route 5's underlying fibre-Habiro idea.

0.verdict: h = 0 kills Delta(net) AND q(q-1) = 0 is a pole of E_0 — degenerate twice

pi/3.verdict: primitive 6th root: q^6-1 = (q^2-1)(q^4+q^2+1) forces q^4+q^2+1 = 0, so Hoefsmit b^2 = 0 and V_(2,1) decouples

5pi/3.verdict: primitive 6th root: q^6-1 = (q^2-1)(q^4+q^2+1) forces q^4+q^2+1 = 0, so Hoefsmit b^2 = 0 and V_(2,1) decouples

assertions.name: reality_is_a_condition_on_the_WHOLE_locus_with_exactly_four_solutions
assertions.detail: Im[q^2-q] factors as -sin(phi) + sin(2*phi); solveset on [0,2pi) gives [0, pi/3, pi, 5*pi/3] — exactly the four expected [0, pi/3, pi, 5*pi/3]. This is a condition at EVERY point of |q|=1, not one imposed only at roots of unity, so the non-rational phases are excluded by reality itself.

assertions.name: dense_scan_finds_no_fifth_zero
assertions.detail: scanned 20000 points on [0,2pi) with sign-change bracketing; found 4 zero(s), each within 1e-15 of one of {0, pi/3, pi, 5pi/3}. An independent check that sympy's solveset is complete — a missed branch would show as an unmatched bracket here.

assertions.name: all_four_reality_solutions_are_degenerate
assertions.detail: phi=0: h = 0 and E_0 has a pole (degenerate twice — #6889 called it 'the pole' and checked only the second); phi=pi: h = 0; phi=pi/3 and 5pi/3: |b^2| < 1e-35, the V_(2,1) coupling vanishes identically at a primitive 6th root. Sixth-root denominators |q^2+1| are non-zero, so the vanishing is the numerator's, not an indeterminate form.

assertions.name: partial_projection_excludes_the_ENTIRE_fibre_locus
assertions.detail: reality cuts |q| = 1 to four points and non-degeneracy removes all four, so under the block's partial projection NO point of the fibre locus survives — not merely no root of unity. This strengthens #6889, whose scope line ('|q| = 1 is a great deal more than its roots of unity') described the non-rational phases as still open when reality had already excluded them.

assertions.name: full_projection_imposes_nothing_so_route5_predicts_nothing_either_way
assertions.detail: |Delta(net) * E_0| evaluated at q = e^(i/7), e^(2i) and the proton q_0 is real in every case (it is a modulus), so a full projection imposes no condition and selects no N. Combined with the assertion above: PARTIAL kills the whole locus, FULL selects nothing — route 5's N-selection mechanism yields no prediction under either reading. Scope-(a) on the MECHANISM; it says nothing about route 5's underlying fibre-Habiro idea.
